3f3aed9ad668eda74e5140d895f2b5d6b5d11271.summary: A tutorial blog post, not a threat report. It walks through a simple proof-of-concept Windows keylogger written in C, which logs keystrokes to a local text file, and says it is for educational purposes. It mentions other malware and groups only in passing, with no analysis of them, and it is not an intelligence report on any actor, campaign or incident.
hedges: This is a practical case for educational purposes only.

3f780cfb0f5b50f46b0ab544610e6279810af77c.summary: Intego's blog post (published 2024-09-05) describes HZ RAT, a macOS remote access Trojan that gives attackers full remote control of infected Macs. The earliest known version was observed in 2022 targeting Windows PCs. The Mac version lists installed apps, collects user information from WeChat and DingTalk, and gathers username and site pairs from Google Password Manager. How victims are infected is not yet known; one known trojanized installer is a modified OpenVPN Connect. The report lists SHA-256 hashes and command-and-control IP addresses, most of which it says appear to be in China.

hedges: It isn't yet known how victims may have encountered HZ RAT installers in the first place.
It's possible that this Trojan horse might be distributed through means such as malicious Google Ads that appear at the top of search results.
Most of the command-and-control IP addresses appear to be located in China.
While the collected Google Password Manager data doesn't include passwords, the username-and-site pairs could potentially be used along with leaked passwords from past data breaches.
